_: Who runs a session, in one place. A desk, its panel and the hub floor show <person>-<n>-<workscope>: the person from the first rule that matches below, n counting that person's sessions in the order they started, the workscope a few words. A session no rule names keeps its callsign (config/callsigns.json), else its title. Rules match, case-insensitive, on the session's title, its code folder and its launch seat (the WORKSPACE_SEAT environment variable). Order: (1) a run below whose match is in the session, then the first of its lanes whose match is also there; (2) a seat that is an org agent (roster key or name): that agent; (3) a gate seat, or the word gate in the title: the gate person.
_roster: The org: agent file name -> the name it goes by. Ships with the CTO org (org/agents). When you rename an agent, add a department or build your own specialist, add it here too (prompts/README.md has the prompt).
_people: Your people: a small sample org. A session shows its person's name large with Department · Focus under it, and the same person live twice is numbered 2, 3, 4 in the order the sessions started. Rename anyone, change their department or focus, or add people (keep the names the roster, the runs and work_words use). A session you open yourself goes to the person whose work_words are in its title, else to everyone_else. Delete people to go back to callsigns.
_gate: The gate is the last check before code reaches main: John, the Chief Engineer, in the CTO org.
_runs: Parallel runs: a run's lanes, so each lane's session is named for the person running it. Empty until you run one. Example: {"run": "Night 1", "match": "night-1", "lanes": [{"match": "lane A", "person": "Cindy", "scope": "API cleanup"}, {"match": "gate", "person": "John", "scope": "Merge gate"}]}
